description: Hardware-agnostic machine learning infrastructure for .NET. Implements high-performance neural network layers in C# that transpile to WebGPU, CUDA, OpenCL, and WebGL via SpawnDev.ILGPU. Optimized for Blazor WebAssembly and native GPU execution.
releaseNotes: v5.2.5 - PERFORMANCE: the browser VAD now KEEPS UP with a live microphone. Silero VAD on WebGPU went from 177.9 ms per frame to 7.81 ms - 0.18x to 4.10x realtime against the 32 ms of audio a 512-sample frame represents - and per-frame host readbacks went from 16 to ZERO. OpenCL improved too: 4.99 ms mean / 47.4 ms p99 to 2.44 / 5.88 (13.1x realtime). Three changes. (1) CAPTURE/REPLAY for SileroVad on CUDA and WebGPU: the graph is identical every frame and every shape is fixed, so the forward is recorded once into a dispatch plan and replayed - 98 dispatches now cost 0.12 ms in a SINGLE interop crossing, against 41 ms of per-node .NET-to-JS encoding before. MEASURED 0.547 ms per node on WebGPU against 0.032 ms on OpenCL, so the gap was never arithmetic. (2) THE LAST READBACKS REMOVED, which is a CORRECTNESS requirement under capture and not merely a cost: promoting a small tensor into runtimeConstants makes the shape interpreter believe it knows the value, so its dispatch is elided - and under capture that FREEZES it at the capture-time value. Silero's adaptive_normalization slices are audio-derived, so every frame normalised against a stale one; segmentation still matched sherpa-onnx 3/3 at 14 ms and only a frame-by-frame probability comparison caught it (0.036 drift by frame 20). ReadbackFeatureOnlyProducers now holds the verified data movers - Concat, Transpose, Squeeze, Unsqueeze, Reshape, Slice - each confirmed by READING its Execute. (3) ONE GPU ROUND TRIP PER FRAME INSTEAD OF TWO: reading a single float the obvious way (stage into a scratch buffer, Synchronize, then CopyToHostAsync) costs a second full round trip on top of the one the replay already paid. The value is now read straight out of the buffer the graph wrote and the recurrent-state copies are queued after it WITHOUT a fence - they are queue-ordered ahead of the next frame's submit, so correctness comes from queue order rather than a wait. That reordering alone was 9.57 to 7.81 ms on WebGPU and 4.25 to 2.44 ms on OpenCL; improving BOTH is the tell that it was waste rather than a browser trick. FIX: a per-call device allocation made CUDA GRAPH CAPTURE IMPOSSIBLE for ANY graph containing a Conv1D. Conv1DKernel.Forward allocated a FRESH device params buffer on every call; Allocate1D is a cuMemAlloc, which is illegal inside a capture window and faults with an ACCESS VIOLATION (0xC0000005) that no try/catch can observe - the process simply dies. Localised with GraphExecutor.CaptureTraceFile, which flushes a line before each node's work so a native fault leaves the offending node as the file's last line: the capture pass died at node 13, the graph's first Conv, with cuMemAlloc_v2 atop the native stack. New Kernels/ParamBufferCache holds one device buffer per DISTINCT param set. A single last-values slot is NOT enough and fails in a way that looks correct - one kernel instance serves every node of its type and their shapes differ, so a warm pass ends with the last node's params resident and the next pass misses on its first. Beyond unblocking capture this removes a cuMemAlloc plus a host-to-device copy per Conv1D call on every backend and stops a retired-buffer list growing for the life of the session. KNOWN: six further per-call allocation sites share that pattern and are NOT yet converted - ColorConversionKernel (2), GatedDeltaNetKernel (1), MissingElementWiseKernels (1), TurboQuantKernels (2). Each blocks CUDA capture for a graph containing it, and ColorConversionKernel sits in the depth pipeline, which does use capture. They are latent rather than observed; ParamBufferCache is the fix to apply. WebGL remains 53.3 ms / 0.60x realtime - capture does not apply there. Full six-backend sweep 4811 passed / 0 failed / 50 skipped. See Changelog.
